items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Roy Eldridge was a member of the band... he went and got his horn and came back and played. Now, here’s one of the greatest trumpet players in the world coming in and playing with me.

ctx.x: Were you playing for predominately black or did you play for white audiences too?

Yes. Some, some. I remember the main dance hall there where all the big bands came to play on the one-nighters, we played there. One night, a very nice band lead by Artie Shaw came and played, and they played from 9-1, and then we played what’s called the “swing shift” from 1-5. So, we were up there playing, and all these guys from Artie Shaw’s band were standing around listening to us, and we thought, well we must be really good [laughs]. Roy Eldridge was a member of the band, and he came to the little joint…
Did you talk to him about playing trumpet?
